newsitem.title: JAPAN: SOCCER-ANTLERS BEAT JEF TO STAY TOP OF J.LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANTLERS BEAT JEF TO STAY TOP OF J.LEAGUE.

text.p: Defending champion Kashima Antlers clinched a comfortable 2-0 victory over JEF United Ichihara late on Wednesday to stay top of the J.League table.
The Antlers broke the deadlock with a spectacular strike in the 39th minute by Tadatoshi Masuda, who skilfully chested down a headed pass from Brazilian striker Bismarck and volleyed it in.
Antlers sealed the match when Bismarck scored in the 53rd minute. It was his third goal in two games.

JEF gave a lacklustre performance and wasted several scoring chances. They played without top striker Yoshika Matsubara, who was suspended for smashing a window at Kobe stadium in a fit of anger last Saturday after being substituted.
The Antlers moved one point clear of second-placed Yokohama Flugels, who handed a humiliating 4-0 defeat to two-time league champions Verdy Kawasaki.
In another match played on Wednesday, Bellmare Hiratsuka emerged as a serious J.League title contender with a 3-0 home win over Kobe Vissel.
With their fourth-consecutive victory, Bellmare moved up to third place, only two points behind the Antlers.
Kashiwa Reysol, which gave up its league lead to the Antlers last weekend, dropped further to sixth place.
Elsewhere, Shimizu S-Pulse edged Fukuoka Avispa 1-0 at home on a goal by Brazilian Alessandro dos Santos, while Nagoya Grampus Eight beat host Kyoto Purple Sanga 3-1.
